items.title: docs: drop the stale benchmark sweeps under docs/benchmarks
items.body:
## Problem

`docs/benchmarks/` holds four sweep write-ups — `mcap-read-threads.md`,
`db3-read-threads.md`, `db3-page-size.md`, and `rewrite-pipeline-baseline.md`.
They were taken against code and fixtures that have since moved on, so the
tables no longer describe what bagwiz does today. A reader who takes them at
face value gets a wrong picture of current performance, which is worse than
having no numbers at all.

## Solution

- Untrack all four files under `docs/benchmarks/`, removing the directory. The
  measurements stay recoverable from git history (`git show <rev>:docs/benchmarks/...`)
  for anyone who needs to look up what was measured when.
- `bagwiz_io/src/io/env_tuning.hpp` cited three of those files to justify the
  `BAGWIZ_READ_THREADS` and `BAGWIZ_DB3_PAGE_SIZE` defaults. Deleting the docs
  would leave those comments pointing at nothing, so the findings that actually
  motivate each default are folded into the comments themselves — the read-thread
  comment now states why 8 sits at the knee (16 regressed on mcap; 4 to 8 bought
  ~2 % wall time for ~26 % more peak RSS on db3), and the page-size comment keeps
  its existing summary with the file pointer dropped. Both rationales now stand
  on their own without an out-of-tree reference.

## Review notes

- No other reference to `docs/benchmarks` exists in the tree; the remaining
  matches for "benchmark" are unrelated (the generic `*/benchmarks/*` cppcheck
  suppression patterns, `scripts/bench-rewrite.sh`, and the word "benchmarking"
  in `docs/environment.md` and `backend_select.hpp`). No markdown link pointed
  at the removed files, so `markdown-link-check` is unaffected.
- No `.gitignore` entry was added for the path. The directory is being retired,
  not made permanently local, and ignoring it would silently swallow a future
  benchmark write-up placed there.
- The only non-docs change is comment text; no code paths, defaults, or limits
  were touched.

## Test plan

- [x] `pre-commit run --files bagwiz_io/src/io/env_tuning.hpp` — clang-format,
      cpplint, cppcheck, and the rest all pass.
- [x] `grep -rn "docs/benchmarks"` over the tree returns nothing.

items.title: fix: rebuild stale benchmark contracts
items.body:
## What changed

- Adds an authenticated, compare-and-swap admin recovery endpoint for stale v3+ benchmark contracts.
- Atomically expires unscored tickets, clears the stale dataset and screened-image binding, and returns the submission to screening.
- Preserves submission, screening, score, and ticket-attempt history while granting each affected validator one clean lease against the replacement contract.

## Why

A v3 ticket can otherwise loop forever when the platform-pinned dataset was generated by a stale data-pipeline image. Releasing or retrying only the ticket reproduces the same mismatch. This recovery forces the required order: fresh screening build and image upload, fresh active-version dataset pin, then fresh v3 ticket issuance.

## Safety

- Requires exact artifact SHA-256, active benchmark version, current dataset SHA-256, and active-version score count.
- Refuses to run while screening is active or after any v3 score has been accepted.
- Does not delete prior screening attempts, scores, or ticket rows.

## Validation

- `uv run pytest -q ditto/tests/api_server/endpoints/test_screener.py` (97 passed)
- `uv run ruff check .`
- `uv run ruff format --check .`
- `git diff --check`

## Rollout prerequisite

Production `ditto-datapipeline` is currently `generate:v0.7.1`; v3 validators use the v0.8.0 generator contract. Build and deploy the immutable v0.8.0 generator image before invoking this repair, or the refreshed dataset will reproduce the same mismatch.

items.title: docs: correct code-health marker taxonomy and stale benchmark claims
items.body:
The docs said **25 markers** in eleven places. `biomarkers/registry.py` registers
**49 detectors** (52 marker ids). They are not interchangeable, and collapsing
them to one number both undercounts the work and hides the part that matters:

| Group | Count | Scores into |
|---|---:|---|
| Defect-scoring | 26 | `defect` (8 of them also `maintainability`) |
| Performance | 20 | `performance` only |
| SQL | 3 | `maintainability` only |
| Governance | 3 | nothing — the finding surfaces, the score is untouched |

Only 26 may move the calibrated number, and that restriction is the point, so
the docs now publish the taxonomy rather than a single figure.

`CODE_HEALTH.md` goes from 944 to 533 lines, restructured from a reference
manual into an argument: how a marker is computed (one pure-AST example, one
call-graph example), what each tier is allowed to affect, how the weights were
calibrated, and what the validation does and does not show. The marker roster
and the per-language detector catalogue move to the architecture companion,
which now carries the full roster and the real category membership.

`INTELLIGENCE_LAYERS.md` keeps the five foundational layers and adds the five
that were shipping undocumented: Change Risk, Test Intelligence, Bug History,
Security and Dead Code. Security had no mention anywhere despite having a
full-history scan with introducing-commit attribution.

### Corrections against live code

- refactoring ships six detectors, not five — `extract_method` was missing
- performance covers 11 dialects / 16 language tags, not 5; category cap is 2.0, not 1.0
- hotspots are decayed-churn percentile plus activity floors, not churn x complexity
- bus factor is authors-to-cover-80%, not a >80% ownership flag
- significant commits retains up to 50, not 10
- decisions are mined from five sources, not eight; three were retired
- hooks: the unconditional pre-search injection was removed on purpose; document the nine behaviours that ship
- dead code excludes 17 dynamic patterns, not 4
- drop the Python filesystem precision (87.6%), the Django batchability split and the "11-repo corpus": no supporting data exists in repowise-bench, only in the docs

### Corrections against the benchmark data

- per-repo AUC tops out at 0.86, not 0.90 — the 0.898 figure is a different corpus and weight set
- within-band AUC is 0.525 / 0.572 / 0.593 / 0.718, not "near 0.49", which came from a superseded quartile cut
- band separation is 16.9x raw and 2.18x size-normalized; publish both, since the raw delta is not significant
- state the LOC tie on discrimination and the Popt loss to a prior-defects baseline
- publish the business-impact non-replication: -0.09 against CodeScene's -0.58

### README

Four claims contradicted the repo's own docs and are fixed: the "only
significant result in the field" superlative (BENCHMARKS says all five tools
reach significance on the main run), the 15/15 adoption figure (BENCHMARKS
formally retracts it), "557 cross-function cases" (the real count is ~90), and
`get_why`'s supersession lineage (no decision edges are written today). The
CodeScene licence row said open source; it is proprietary with on-prem Docker.
The headline now leads with the five layers instead of a compression number, the
superseded n=15 agent-loop result is replaced by the n=43 run, and the 135x
default-mode index cost sits next to the 22x.

Marker counts also swept out of `docs/README.md`, `CLI_REFERENCE.md`,
`COMMERCIAL.md`, both plugin skill files, and the three SVG assets that had the
number baked in as text.

### Checks

Internal link and anchor validation passes across all five touched docs,
including the two anchors `docs/architecture/code-health.md` depends on.
Docs-only plus one generator string; no runtime code touched.

### Known gap

`LANGUAGE_SUPPORT.md` says 18 languages; the registry has 19 AST-capable, and
that doc disagrees with itself (13 Full + 4 Good + 1 Partial, then "all twelve"
below the table). Left as-is here rather than fixing one doc and not the
authority doc — worth its own pass.

items.title: Gate adoption bands against the declared scale, and reband 13 stale benchmarks
items.body:
## The gap this closes

`adoption_bands` are declared per product type in `sources/rubrics/*.yaml`, serialized into `currentai.registry.adoption_bands`, and read by the scoring SQL. Tests covered the declaration's shape and the serializer's output.

**Nothing ever compared a product's recorded `(level, reach)` against them.** The bands were authoritative for the warehouse and advisory for the corpus — the hand-mirrored-logic drift `check_parity` exists to catch, one axis over. 217 of 432 banded products were off-scale when first measured.

`dataset.yaml` predicted it in a comment: *"14 dataset products record level 4 against a reach of 1M-10M, which is level 5 on this scale ... They are a work list, not a migration."* A work list in a comment is not a gate, so it grew instead of shrinking.

## `build/check_adoption.py`

Checks two things:

1. the reach label is one the applicable scale declares
2. the recorded level is the level that label denotes

Scale resolution is keyed on `(product_type, signal_type)`, not type alone, because `stars_fallback` has its own labels and its own ceiling of 3 — a star is not a use.

Report-only by default, like `check_freshness`. Gating today would fail on a backlog that predates the bands existing, and a gate that fails on day one teaches people to skip it.

## Fixed here: 217 → 166

**38 case-only labels** normalized (`10k-100k` → `10K-100K`). No level moved.

**13 benchmark corpora** re-verified against live Hugging Face figures and rebanded onto the dataset scale — whose top band is `>1M`, one order of magnitude below software and model, because no dataset artifact in the corpus has ever exceeded 10M.

Three moved **level**, not just label:

```
mmlu       5/'>10M'    -> 4/'100K-1M'   on   477,890 monthly downloads
mmmu       4/'1M-10M'  -> 3/'10K-100K'  on    51,058
evalplus   4/'1M-10M'  -> 3/'10K-100K'  on    51,081  (HumanEval+ and MBPP+ summed)
```

`mmlu` was the worst of them: it claimed the top band and a reach of `>10M` against a real figure of 477,890, and its own note argued *"Level 5 on download volume"*.

All 13 now carry `last_verified` plus `http_status` and `content_sha256` from a live read through `build.fetch_source`, so `check_refetch` can later prove the read was real. Those bodies carry a download counter and drift between any two requests — `check_refetch` documents that case and never fails on drift.

**Real `last_verified` coverage: 180 → 193 axes.**

## Deliberately not fixed — see #223

The remaining 166 need a ruling, not a correction. 58 `stars_fallback` products record download-vocabulary labels, and their levels don't follow the stars scale either (`bigcodebench` records level 2 on 503 stars; the scale says 1). Rebanding them would move published adoption levels on dozens of products, which feeds the gap map's maturity signal. That's a methodology decision.

## Test plan

- `pytest` — 461 passed, plus `tests/test_check_adoption.py` (5 new)
- `validate`, `check_recipe`, `check_rubric`, `check_components`, `check_routing`, `check_capability`, `check_verification`, `check_retirement`, `check_adoption` — all green
- The new tests pin the 13 refreshed corpora and their `last_verified`, so they cannot silently drift back
- Generated files not committed (bot-owned)

One thing caught in review of my own work: the first attempt wrote `establishes: [adoption]` onto the new sources, which `validate` rejected — `establishes` names a scoring dimension, not an axis. Stripped rather than re-fetched, so the figures on record are the ones reported above.

The comment at `ci-nightly.yml:248-254` justified `continue-on-error: true` on the benchmark comparison by claiming the baseline `v0.9.0.json` was a fabricated placeholder. items.title: chore(npm): drop hardcoded rule count and stale benchmark from the package description
items.body:
The published npm description reads:

> "Open detection standard -- like Sigma, but for AI agents. **751 rules** for prompt injection, tool poisoning, context exfiltration, and MCP attacks. Shipped in Cisco AI Defense. **97.2% recall on NVIDIA garak**."

Both numbers are wrong on the registry right now. The corpus is at 780 on `main` (770 effective), and garak was re-measured to 91.5% on 2026-07-28.

Neither can be kept correct by updating it. The rule count moves most days via auto-crystallize and ecosystem PRs, while the registry description only refreshes on publish — so any number written here is stale between releases by construction. The benchmark has the same problem plus a worse failure mode: a recall figure that drifts upward in a reader's memory while the measured value goes down.

This removes both rather than refreshing them. `data/stats.json` and the README badges stay the place where a current number lives, and they move with the corpus.

Note: the registry listing only changes on the next publish, so this PR fixes the source, not the live description.

## Summary

Fixes 2 findings from a swarm audit of `providers/` and `scorer/`/`benchmark/`:

items.body:
## Summary

Fixes `benchmarks/latency.ts` import paths broken by the `src/core/` restructure and adds CI coverage so benchmark import/type drift is caught before merge.

- Correct 4 stale imports to `src/core/...` (`pinecone-client`, `client-context`, `namespaces-cache`, `guided-query-tool`)
- Add `benchmarks/tsconfig.json` (`noEmit`, extends root) and `npm run typecheck:benchmarks`
- Add offline `npm run benchmark:smoke` (`--smoke`: WARMUP=1, ITERATIONS=3, no `baseline.json`, skips `query_with_rerank`)
- Wire both checks into `npm run ci` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

## Related issue

- Close https://github.com/cppalliance/pinecone-read-only-mcp-typescript/issues/208

## Why

Root `tsconfig.json` only includes `src/**/*`, so `npm run typecheck` never compiled `benchmarks/`. The harness still pointed at pre-restructure paths and failed at module resolution; CI had no step to catch it.

## CI changes

| Step | Command |
|------|---------|
| Type check benchmarks | `npm run typecheck:benchmarks` (after main typecheck) |
| Benchmark smoke run | `npm run benchmark:smoke` (after CLI smoke test) |

Emit output is unchanged: benchmark typecheck uses a separate `noEmit` project; `dist/` remains scoped to `src/`.

## Smoke mode behavior

`--smoke` is network-free for CI:

- Skips `query_with_rerank` — the bench double’s `rerankResults` override is dead post-restructure; rerank now goes through `rerankResultsImpl(this.indexSession.ensureClient(), …)` and would hit real Pinecone HTTP
- Bootstraps dummy `PINECONE_API_KEY` / `PINECONE_INDEX_NAME` so legacy `ServerContext` config resolution works offline

Full `npm run benchmark` (non-smoke) still runs all scenarios including `query_with_rerank`.

## Follow-up (out of scope)

- `scripts/test-search.ts` has the same class of stale imports and is not typechecked
